Mayor Szabó Ferenc's report of 25 April 1944: the city had 1,950 Jews, per list compiled by the Jewish Council (Mandel Sándor) from 18 April; ghetto set up around Csarnok/Horánszky/Pillangó streets incl. synagogue and school

June 1944: 4,666 Jews held in the sugar-factory collection camp, about half from Szolnok, rest from Jász-Nagykun-Szolnok and Békés localities; 29 died there; two transports (first ~2,700 on 25 June) to Strasshof and Auschwitz. Camp count incl. deportees from elsewhere

After the German invasion (19 March 1944) the 1,800 remaining Jews in Szolnok were confined in a ghetto and at the end of June deported to Auschwitz and Austria
The former community numbered about 2,000 ('kétezer főt számláló egykori közösség'); 800 did not return (Holocaust deaths, not population). Community built the town from 1840; large synagogue 1896

June 1944: Jews from the downtown ghetto and surrounding settlements crowded into the sugar factory; c.5,000 people from fifteen settlements, sent to Auschwitz or labor camps near Vienna (regional collection count)
4,700 people crowded into sugar-factory quarters built for 400-500 seasonal workers for 10-12 days; two trains, to Strasshof and Auschwitz-Birkenau (regional collection count)
Survivor diary (Erdős Gáspár): some 6,000 people crammed into the sugar factory area in June 1944 (regional collection count, estimate)
1944: Szolnok became a 'labor camp' and concentration point for Hungarian Jews being deported to Austria
